title: The Arnolfini Portrait
source: National Gallery, London (public domain). Download the full-resolution file from Wikimedia Commons: Van_Eyck_-_Arnolfini_Portrait.jpg
caption: A 1434 painting with a reflection, a signature written like graffiti and a single candle burning in daylight. Which detail did you miss? #art #arthistory #painting #history #oilpainting

slides.headline: This 1434 painting hides its painter in a mirror
slides.sub: Jan van Eyck, The Arnolfini Portrait, 1434

slides.headline: Look at the mirror
slides.text: The convex mirror shows the room from behind, including two tiny figures in the doorway. One of them may be Van Eyck himself.

slides.headline: “Johannes de eyck fuit hic 1434”
slides.text: “Jan van Eyck was here, 1434.” Written on the wall like graffiti, not like a normal signature. Many read it as the painter declaring he was a witness.

slides.headline: 10 scenes the size of a fingernail
slides.text: The mirror's frame holds ten tiny scenes from the Passion of Christ.

slides.headline: One candle, in daylight
slides.text: A single candle burns in the chandelier at midday. What it means is still debated.

slides.headline: Oranges as a status symbol
slides.text: In 15th-century Bruges, oranges were an expensive import. Leaving them by the window was a quiet show of wealth.

slides.headline: Shoes off
slides.text: A pair of wooden pattens lies on the floor. Some see sacred ground, others simple everyday life.

slides.headline: The little dog
slides.text: A small lap dog, often read as a symbol of fidelity, and a luxury only the rich could keep.

slides.headline: She is not pregnant
slides.text: She is holding up the heavy folds of a fashionable gown. The rounded silhouette was the style of the time.
